title: El del parque
goal: Get away from a friendly drunk without insulting him
culture: He is harmless and the whole park knows him. Walking off mid-sentence is what a chele does, and the doñas on the benches will see you do it. Leaving properly is a set of fixed phrases and it costs you thirty seconds.

beats.es: ¡Amigo! ¡Amigo, venga! Yo trabajé ocho años en Miami. Allá sí se gana bien, ¿oyó?
beats.good: Así es agrees with the claim without joining the story, and echoing his number back shows you were listening. Contradicting a drunk is the long way home.

beats.es: Regáleme veinte pesos, hermano, para un fresco. Nada más veinte.
beats.objective: Say you have nothing on you
beats.en: I haven’t got anything on me, brother.
beats.good: No ando con nada is honest and unarguable. No tengo invites a discussion about your shoes.

beats.es: Ah, ni modo. Pero óigame esta otra, una historia buenísima...
beats.objective: Leave, but leave the door open
beats.say: Ya me voy. Otro día conversamos.
beats.en: I’m off now. We’ll talk another day.
ok: ya me voy otro dia conversamos
beats.good: Ya me voy on its own is abrupt. Otro día conversamos turns leaving into a plan, and he will hold you to it.

beats.es: ¡Vaya pues! Es usted buena gente, hermano.
beats.good: Both at once is the full goodbye: cuídese looks after him, que le vaya bien wishes the rest of his day well. It is what stops leaving reading as escaping.
